clue.text: This is liquid in the main

definitions.text: This is liquid in the main

parts.words: This is liquid in the main
parts.note: the main is an old poetic name for the open ocean, so the liquid found there is what the clue describes

explanation.walkthrough: 'The main' sounds like a water main or the main part of something, but here it is the high seas.
explanation.definitionFit: The ocean, poetically the main, is filled with salt brine from the waves.

clue.text: Poles at church for only a brief spell

parts.note: S and N are the south and north poles

explanation.surface: Polish people attend church only briefly.
explanation.definitionFit: A short burst of something, like a fragment of song, is a brief bit.

clue.text: Like a carrier getting lost

parts.note: as means like, in the manner of
a tray is used to carry dishes

explanation.surface: A delivery firm or courier goes missing.
explanation.definitionFit: Gone off course or wandering from the right path means mislaid.

clue.text: Instruction given to musicians, legal or otherwise

indicators.note: otherwise means in a different form, so the letters are set in a new order

explanation.surface: A direction for players, lawful or not.
explanation.definitionFit: This Italian tempo marking tells players to perform briskly and lively.

clue.text: See some nightdresses, pyjamas and nightshirts

indicators.note: only some of the letters of the following words are taken, a run within them

explanation.surface: Look at a selection of sleepwear.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across the end of 'nightdresses' and the start of 'pyjamas'.
explanation.definitionFit: To catch sight of or spot something is to see it.

clue.text: The person taking much interest in financial dealings

definitions.text: The person taking much interest in financial dealings

parts.words: The person taking much interest in financial dealings
parts.note: reads as someone keen on finance, but interest here is the charge on a loan, and much of it means extortionate lending

explanation.walkthrough: 'Interest' looks like enthusiasm; it is the money charged on a loan.
explanation.definitionFit: A moneylender who charges excessive rates on loans is the classic figure described.

clue.text: Skill in bridge demonstrated by a tough character

indicators.note: the skill sits within the bridge word, enclosed by it

parts.note: a span is a bridge or the arch of one
art means skill or craft

explanation.surface: A hardy person shows talent at the card game of bridge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bridge' suggests the card game, which the surface leans on with 'skill'; here it is a structure across a gap.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone austere and hardy, like the disciplined citizens of ancient Sparta.

clue.text: Left to cut the long grass talked about

indicators.note: one word cuts into the other, splitting it open

parts.note: a reed is a tall grass growing by water
port is the left side of a ship

explanation.surface: Someone was left to mow the tall grass, so people gossiped.
explanation.definitionFit: Something told or described in a news account has been related.

clue.text: Hurt constituents without being malevolent

indicators.note: the parts of the word are taken separately and reassembled in another order

parts.note: less means lacking, as in pointless

explanation.surface: Wounded voters lose any spite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Constituents' rearranges HURT; 'being' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Showing no pity or mercy, someone cruel acts with ill will.

clue.text: Seen before run as a fast mover

parts.note: ante is Latin for before, as in ante-room
to lope is to run with long easy strides

explanation.surface: Something was spotted running ahead, quick on its feet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Seen' and 'as' are only link words here.
explanation.definitionFit: This African grazing animal is famous for its speed when fleeing predators.

clue.text: Have a little drink with a loved one in a flap

parts.note: to lap is to drink with the tongue, a little at a time, like a cat
a pet is a darling or favourite person

explanation.surface: Someone sips a drink with their sweetheart while in a state of agitation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In a flap' looks like panic, but the flap is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a loose fold or hanging piece of material on a garment or headdress.

clue.text: Standard nowadays, and neat, which is an absurdity

parts.note: par is the standard or normal level
AD, anno domini, marks the present era
neat is an old word for cattle, so an ox

explanation.surface: Today's norms and tidiness are ridiculous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Neat' looks like tidy; it is the old word for cattle.
explanation.definitionFit: A self-contradictory statement that seems ridiculous yet may be true.

clue.text: Direct payment called for

definitions.meaning: to direct as a verb, meaning to instruct or command someone formally
the price or fee asked for something

explanation.definitionFit: A judge instructs a jury, and a shop asks a fee; the one word covers both senses.

clue.text: Minister at the head of a sovereign country

indicators.note: the minister is placed in front of what follows, leading the rest

parts.note: a pastor is a minister in charge of a church
a sovereign is a gold pound coin, and L is the abbreviation for pound

explanation.surface: A clergyman serves as ruler of an independent nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sovereign country' reads as one state; split it: sovereign is the pound L and country is the definition, an adjective as in country life.
explanation.definitionFit: Rural, rustic scenes of shepherds and fields are described by this adjective.

clue.text: Strip fixed under sea-going craft

indicators.note: something fixed is repaired or rearranged, so the letters are put in new order

parts.note: SS stands for steamship

explanation.surface: Bare a part repaired beneath a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: To take off one's clothes is to strip.

clue.text: Would-be top people?

parts.note: sounds like social climbers aspiring to the elite, but the top here is a literal summit they hope to reach

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests ambitious social climbers; these climbers want the top of a peak.
explanation.definitionFit: Climbers of peaks aim to stand on the summit, the very top.

clue.text: Bill, the dog, scoffed. That's nice!

parts.note: AC is short for account, a bill
a cur is a mongrel dog
to scoff is to eat greedily, so ate

explanation.surface: Bill's dog wolfed it down, and the owner approved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nice' is in its old sense of precise or exact, as in a nice distinction.
explanation.definitionFit: Exact, precise and correct in detail, like a fine distinction.

clue.text: Friend accommodating rebel leader in a pickle

indicators.note: accommodating means housing, so one word holds the other inside

parts.note: a mate is a friend

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A pal shelters a rebel chief who is in trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In a pickle' looks like trouble; RINA goes inside MATE and pickle is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To soak food in a seasoned liquid is to steep or cure it.

clue.text: Teachers' hour for correction in school

indicators.note: letters needing correction are put right by rearranging them into a new order

explanation.surface: Staff at a school set aside an hour to mark work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For correction' rearranges TEACHERS and HOUR. Charterhouse is a well-known English public school in Surrey.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the name of a famous independent boarding school in Godalming.

clue.text: Many will be absorbed by the novel 'Hatred' — it's by Arnold Bennett

indicators.note: one thing taken into another ends up inside it
novel means new, so the letters are made into a new arrangement

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, so many

explanation.surface: A review praises a novel called Hatred written by Arnold Bennett.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel' looks like a book; it rearranges HATRED. Arnold Bennett was an English novelist of the Potteries.
explanation.definitionFit: Bennett wrote a 1911 comic novel of this title about Denry Machin.

clue.text: Remaining and bearing up

definitions.meaning: supporting with stays, as a mast or a corset is braced

explanation.definitionFit: One sense is to stop and stay on; the other is to prop with ropes or stays.

clue.text: A stone of fish after making the required deduction

parts.note: the gar is a long-snouted fish
net is what is left after deductions, as with net pay

explanation.surface: A gem is worth its weight in fish once tax is taken off.
explanation.definitionFit: A deep red semi-precious gem used in jewellery.

clue.text: Oriental copper — the fellow's forward

parts.note: a sen is a small copper coin of Japan and other Far Eastern countries
a don is a university fellow; the 's is just the link

explanation.surface: An Eastern policeman is the man in front.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' looks like a police officer but is a coin.
explanation.definitionFit: To pass mail on to a new address is to forward it.

clue.text: The sphere of one Parisian and four Irish

parts.note: un is French for one, as said in Paris
IV is four in Roman numerals
Erse is the Gaelic language of Ireland

explanation.surface: A domain shared by a Frenchman and a group of four Irish people.
explanation.definitionFit: The cosmos, everything that exists, is the whole sphere of being.

clue.text: Injury that's made a mother appear older

parts.note: a dam is the mother of an animal, especially a horse
to age is to grow or look older

explanation.surface: Some harm has made a mum look older than her years.
explanation.definitionFit: Harm or physical hurt done to something is described by this word.

clue.text: Man concerned with present

parts.note: he stands for a man
re means about, concerning

explanation.surface: A man is interested in the gift.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in attendance at this spot means being present.

clue.text: Articles to be read about obnoxious place in Iran

indicators.note: the two articles go around the outside of the other word, enclosing it

parts.note: a and an are the two indefinite articles of English
bad means nasty or offensive

explanation.surface: Newspaper pieces about a nasty spot in Iran.
explanation.walkthrough: Abadan is an oil-refining city in south-west Iran; 'to be read' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a port city in Khuzestan province, home to a major oil refinery.

clue.text: Handed over as authorised, but not for the first time

parts.note: re- is the prefix meaning again, so not for the first time
signed means approved with a signature

explanation.surface: A document was passed on as approved, though it had been signed before.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as RE-SIGNED: signed again; the whole word means gave up a post.
explanation.definitionFit: To quit a job is to give up, surrender or hand over the post.

clue.text: Notes outside men second reforms

indicators.note: the notes go round the next word, one on each side

parts.note: E and D are both musical notes
taken as written

explanation.surface: Memos about staff are being revised again.
explanation.definitionFit: To correct or revise a text is to improve or make better.

clue.text: A number will be fed into poultry to increase the size

indicators.note: food fed into a bird goes inside it, so one word is put within the other

parts.note: a hen is a domestic fowl, a piece of poultry
eight is a number

explanation.surface: Fattening chickens by feeding them extra numbers to make them grow bigger.
explanation.definitionFit: To raise or intensify something is to make it greater or taller.
